lines: CASTLE LENDING LIBRARY. CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE COUNCIL UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE.
The key is kept with the key to the forest gate, on the council's green tag. Enquiries to the Museum, ten until four.
CASTLE LENDING LIBRARY. Tuesday to Saturday, nine until six. The STACKS off the LENDING DESK; the READING ROOM and REFERENCE off the STACKS, and REFERENCE opens onto the LENDING DESK as well.
Books are not to leave the building. After six, readers are asked not to leave it either, and the doors are locked to help them.
Underneath, in pencil, pressed hard: the roof came in on the fourteenth. nobody has been up to look.
Every page has been cut out close to the spine with a blade, neatly, by somebody who had the time. One's left.
It's about seeds, written for somebody who has never grown one. SOW THINLY. COVER WITH THEIR OWN DEPTH OF SOIL. WATER FROM BELOW.
The last line is Julie's small slanting hand: it will not come up in the dark. Do it by day.
The page says the same thing. I run my thumb down the cut edges, and they're all one length.
Somebody's had a fire going on the reading room floor, and swept the ash into the grate after. The boards round it have been scrubbed.
They burned the chairs, every one, and not a single book. I can sleep here.
LENDING DESK. Tickets are to be shown going out, and coming in.
STACKS. The library steps are to be put back on their mark after use. Readers are not to climb the shelves.
READING ROOM. Silence, please, at all times.
Somebody has underlined at all times, twice.
REFERENCE. Books are not to be taken out.
Under it, in pencil: one left, on the top shelf. The roof came in over it on the fourteenth.
